args.summary: 63F returning to the ED with dyspnea again. She has had 2 weeks of dyspnea and cough. A right thoracentesis drained 1.5 L of milky fluid and helped only briefly. The fluid shows a chylothorax: TG 434 mg/dL, cholesterol 154 mg/dL, 82% lymphocytes, low LDH and protein, and cytology negative. There was no trauma or surgery, so this is a nontraumatic chylothorax that has quickly come back. CT shows enlarged lymph nodes in both hila and the mediastinum, severe narrowing of the right middle lobe bronchus, partial lung collapse and infiltrates. This points to blockage of the thoracic duct or lymph channels by a mediastinal disease process. At the initial visit she was breathing fast but oxygen was normal. Repeat-visit exam details were not supplied.

args.rationale: Right chylothorax (TG 434 mg/dL) that came back quickly after 1.5 L was drained. It is caused by biopsy-proven extensive-stage small cell lung cancer with bilateral hilar and mediastinal adenopathy. CT also shows severe narrowing of the right middle lobe bronchus with partial collapse and infiltrates. The effusion has recurred and is causing symptoms. There is also a risk of post-obstructive pneumonia and of nutritional and immune losses from the chyle. Repeat-visit vitals were not supplied. She needs inpatient pleural management and prompt start of systemic cancer treatment.
args.followup_or_handoff: Admit to medicine/oncology with continuous SpO2 monitoring. Repeat therapeutic thoracentesis. If fluid reaccumulates quickly, place an indwelling pleural catheter or consider pleurodesis. Start a low-fat/MCT diet and give nutrition support. Consult oncology urgently to start platinum-etoposide plus immunotherapy, since treating the tumor is the main way to control the chylothorax. Order a staging brain MRI. Check CBC, CMP, sodium (SIADH), albumin and lymphocytes. Watch for post-obstructive pneumonia and treat with antibiotics if it develops. Consider interventional pulmonology for the RML airway narrowing. Discuss goals of care with the patient and family.
